answer: A bond is refunded only after 30 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. The ivory counter is kept in saffron and beacon publishes each reset. A hostile operator therefore has to keep each alias continuously active for 30 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 8 epochs. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
